Let's take this one: https://hoodi.etherscan.io/tx/0x2cc3443005219277098374b0ce77b7c6a6a1e06b1084721b77ea87bc780d3e00#authorizationlist The TX has nonce 25 and the code authorization has nonce 25 too. Both operations (tx & authorization) require their own nonce and increase it by 1 after processing. To make that work, you need to increase the nonce of your authorization by one. So the tx has nonce 25 and the authorization nonce 26. You wallet's nonce is increased by 2 at the end. Right now your authorizations are ignored because the nonce is too low Thank you ! <@808969530608451584> . Really appreciate the warm response. T_T that made alot of sense. So i tried on sepholia this time so that i could actually make use of tenderly to view the transaction. i've updated my tuple creation function: ``` async function createAuthTuple(wallet, chainId, contractAddress, nonce) { let authNonce = nonce + 1; // Increment nonce by 1 for the next transaction const chainIdHex = "0x" + chainId.toString(16); const nonceHex = "0x" + authNonce.toString(16); const addressHex = contractAddress; // Should already be a hex string like "0x..." // Step 1: RLP encode [chain_id, address, nonce] const rlpEncoded = RLP.encode([chainIdHex, addressHex, nonceHex]); // Step 2: Prepend MAGIC (0x05) const magic = Buffer.from('05', 'hex'); const messageBuffer = Buffer.concat([magic, rlpEncoded]); // Step 3: Hash to get the message const message = ethers.keccak256(messageBuffer); // Step 4: Sign the message const signature = await wallet.signMessage(ethers.getBytes(message)); const sig = ethers.Signature.from(signature); const yParity = sig.v - 27; // Converts v to 0 or 1 // Step 5: Return the tuple return [ chainIdHex, addressHex, nonceHex, yParity, sig.r, sig.s ]; } ``` This is the transaction hash for tx2: `0xe83c5c931d6454d7060b0d8ee4bc3582bf303a6c3d978ca668166fcdb49aa8fe` on sepolia it should trigger a transfer that would send 0.1 eth to 0x6aE2F56C057e31a18224DBc6Ae32B0a5FBeDFCB0 good thing now is that i can see the trasferETH function being called .. but the state did not change for the wallet address `0x6aE2F56C057e31a18224DBc6Ae32B0a5FBeDFCB0` it should trigger a transfer from Wallet A `0x3b98517FC209671AeA5d22a58e068f5a7Eab03A8`(context of the smart contract) to Wallet B (`0x6aE2F56C057e31a18224DBc6Ae32B0a5FBeDFCB0`).. if i understood correctly .. Etherscan should show the delegation address on the wallet overview when set: https://hoodi.etherscan.io/address/0x9f53917b21852c66dfc572c4807c90bfc39351ec (see the delegated addresss entry under more info) i transacted on sepholia let me try hoodi.. you are right ! there's no delegated address ! in wallet A `0x3b98517FC209671AeA5d22a58e068f5a7Eab03A8` https://hoodi.etherscan.io/tx/0x95a5fc2508aa9580ba5072e579483f50e89cfa3a4bb22a6dbe6641a09ae4423a#authorizationlist but the nonce for the authList is correct now ... its + 1 of the transaction nonce. hmm, it looks all right 🤔 I think there's something bad with the signature.. Everything else looks good how does your `messageBuffer` look like before hashing? can you print it for comparison? 🙂 oh, I think `ethers.signMessage` is not a low level signer. WOO HOOO !!! https://hoodi.etherscan.io/address/0x3b98517FC209671AeA5d22a58e068f5a7Eab03A8 ``` async function createAuthTuple(wallet, chainId, contractAddress, nonce) { let authNonce = nonce + 1; // Increment nonce by 1 for the next transaction const chainIdHex = "0x" + chainId.toString(16); const nonceHex = "0x" + authNonce.toString(16); const addressHex = contractAddress; // Should already be a hex string like "0x..." // Step 1: RLP encode [chain_id, address, nonce] const rlpEncoded = RLP.encode([chainIdHex, addressHex, nonceHex]); // Step 2: Prepend MAGIC (0x05) const magic = Buffer.from('05', 'hex'); const messageBuffer = Buffer.concat([magic, rlpEncoded]); // Step 3: Hash to get the message const message = ethers.keccak256(messageBuffer); // Step 4: Sign the message const walletSigningKey = new ethers.SigningKey(wallet.privateKey); const authSignature = walletSigningKey.sign(ethers.getBytes(message)); // const signature = await wallet.signMessage(ethers.getBytes(message)); const sig = ethers.Signature.from(authSignature); const yParity = sig.v - 27; // Converts v to 0 or 1 // Step 5: Return the tuple return [ chainIdHex, addressHex, nonceHex, yParity, sig.r, sig.s ]; } ``` updated authTuple function ! used the primitive sign function . <@808969530608451584> thank you 3000

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content:
Your authorizations have a too low nonce.

Let's take this one:
https://hoodi.etherscan.io/tx/0x2cc3443005219277098374b0ce77b7c6a6a1e06b1084721b77ea87bc780d3e00#authorizationlist

The TX has nonce 25 and the code authorization has nonce 25 too.
Both operations (tx & authorization) require their own nonce and increase it by 1 after processing.

To make that work, you need to increase the nonce of your authorization by one.
So the tx has nonce 25 and the authorization nonce 26. 
You wallet's nonce is increased by 2 at the end.

Right now your authorizations are ignored because the nonce is too low
